Last week, I tilled and expanded my garden plot (now 1200 square feet). I'd been worried because it's nearly May and I don't have anything in the ground there because we'd keep getting cold spells down to the high 30s but it's still later than I planted last year.

Went out yesterday to check the plot to make sure it wasn't ready to sprout a new, fresh lawn (it's trying) and noticed some seedlings popping up... sunflower seeds from last year have just started to sprout. Looks like they're about 5 days old. Small enough to transplant to the new area but also a great reminder that I'm not behind according to the weather.

In other news, I have 5 less sunflowers to plant this year...

Today I'll be planting a couple of apple trees, a peach tree, a blueberry bush, two raspberry bushes, a blackberry bush, 2 grape vines, and two olive trees. Not sure the olive trees will do well but why not, right? If it works, I'll have fresh olives. If not, they were only $10 each.

I figure I'll train the grapes along two lengths of my fence (and leave the third for the morning glories that will pop up soon).

We have cilantro that is outgrowing its pot 2 weeks after planting, dill that is doing great, and some other herbs. The oregano from last year is growing like a weed and the sage from last year is doing great too. The strawberries survived the winter fine and my parsley from last year is getting huge and oddly not flowering to go to seed.

Roses are doing okay though I trimmed them a couple weeks late but they're utterly filled with buds.

Oh, and the rhubarb plant popped up from nowhere and grew two inches in a week.

And finally, was digging in the plot yesterday and found oodles of earthworms... and a few Japanese beetle grubs - they're fuckin' huge this year. Seeing them so huge so early means we'll get them a little earlier and I expect swarms and swarms of them (they love roses). I'd treat the yard but it'll do no good with how many there are everywhere else. So it looks like more bug spray this summer to keep them from killing my everythings.

At least there's no termites so I have that going for me.

Oh, shit, almost forgot... got the freeze dryer I'd been planning on getting but the vacuum pump had been dropped before shipping, the hose has a leak. They've replaced the pump and sending a replacement hose. The initial vacuum test went great so I know the main unit and pump works. No more "Cook everything before it goes bad" this year.

Really want a crab apple tree this year, maybe I'll order one online or something.
I'd been flipping out because I thought I was behind on planting because we'd get a very cold spell for 2 or 3 days every other week. Last year's garden reminded me otherwise.

I usually just go with whatever nature says and nature has been telling me that it's too cold.
